# Neutral governance and onboarding decisions

Prepared policies exist; no foundation governance or accountable external maintainer has been conferred.

1. Aksum would offer Apache-2.0 original code, contracts, tests, corpus and documentation. Ancillary schema terms stay separate and require foundation review.
2. Eligible maintainers should be selected through real contributions and technical/security review, with organizations represented transparently. No contributor slots are invented.
3. Changes use PR review, CI and semantic versioning. Schema/corpus/contract changes require independent semantics and rights review; failures are not hidden by editing expectations.
4. Owner chooses accountable humans and a security responder. The publisher bot is automation only. Actual prior response behavior cannot be asserted.
5. LFDT requires DCO on all imported code commits. Current corporate attribution is not a DCO attestation. Only a legally authorized human may provide the import sign-off or solicit actual contributor attestations.
6. New naming, repository hosting/transfer, domains and trademarks are negotiated after acceptance. Any Contribution Agreement requires the real entity signatory. This package approves no transfer.
7. Do not designate the machine-readable engineering contracts as a formal CSL specification to bypass a rights issue. If standards work becomes a separate activity, assess the CSL framework explicitly.

Primary process: https://github.com/LF-Decentralized-Trust/lab-proposals
Charter: https://github.com/LF-Decentralized-Trust-labs/governance/blob/main/lf-decentralized-trust-labs_Charter.pdf
